// GENERATED BY genbodies.py -- DO NOT EDIT BY HAND.
//
// `user` and archived, so a choice follows the player and survives a restart.

// Which body to wear. A name from a VRAVATAR lump; empty means none, and with none nothing
// is spawned, drawn or hooked -- the mod is inert.
user string vr_avatar = "c_doom_marine";

// Draw the WHOLE body from your own eyes, rather than only the hands and forearms.
//
// Off by default: until the arm solve lands (M3) the arms follow the hands rigidly, and a
// torso attached to them is visibly wrong seen from the inside. This exists so a body can
// be looked at on purpose anyway.
//
// It does not affect a mirror, a spectator or another player -- they always see the whole
// body, because what is hidden is decided per view, not in the pose.
user bool vr_avatar_fullbody = false;

// Draw the avatar's joints as axes (level 2 of the rig debug drawing).
user bool vr_avatar_debug = false;

// The in-game mirror. It hangs itself in front of you when you switch it on and stays put,
// so you can walk up to it and turn side-on -- which is most of what a mirror is for.
//
// A MONITOR, NOT A REFLECTION, and deliberately: the camera stands at the panel and TRACKS
// you, so you stay in frame while you walk, crouch and lean. A true reflection loses you the
// moment you step aside, which is exactly when you were trying to look at yourself.
//
// It renders the whole scene a second time. Switch it on to check something, off after.
user bool vr_mirror = false;
user float vr_mirror_dist = 96.0;       // how far in front of you it stands
user float vr_mirror_up = 34.0;         // its centre above your feet
user float vr_mirror_fov = 70.0;        // how much of you it takes in
user float vr_mirror_standoff = 8.0;    // camera clear of its own panel; see mirror.zs

// ---- the body fit (VR_BODY_HANDS_SPEC.md M3 task 3) ------------------------
//
// Measured off the player by `vr_fitmode body`: stand straight, both arms out to the sides,
// hold the trigger. Everything downstream scales from these two -- the avatar's world scale,
// and how far the arm solver reaches.
//
// Zero means never fitted. The engine then assumes the player is built like the body he is
// wearing, which is visibly wrong for a tall player on a short model and honest about it
// rather than quietly guessing.
user float vr_fit_height = 0.0;      // eye height standing, metres
user float vr_fit_armspan = 0.0;     // wrist to wrist, arms out, metres

// ---- fit mode storage (VR_BODY_HANDS_SPEC.md C.5) --------------------------
//
// Six numbers as one string: "x y z pitch yaw roll". Offsets are in the hand frame;
// rotations apply pitch about X, yaw about Z, roll about Y, in that order.
//
// ONE STRING AND NOT SIX CVARS: forty-two cvars for seven bodies is a config file nobody
// can read, and the six are only ever set or cleared together.
//
// Empty means never fitted, which is not an error -- the engine then uses the fit derived
// from the model's own measurements (spec B.5).

user string vr_fit_hand_c_doom_marine_R = "";
user string vr_fit_hand_c_doom_marine_L = "";

user string vr_fit_hand_dark_ages_praetor_R = "";
user string vr_fit_hand_dark_ages_praetor_L = "";

user string vr_fit_hand_doomslayer_default_R = "";
user string vr_fit_hand_doomslayer_default_L = "";

user string vr_fit_hand_lillwasa_doomguy_R = "";
user string vr_fit_hand_lillwasa_doomguy_L = "";

user string vr_fit_hand_marine_guy_classic_R = "";
user string vr_fit_hand_marine_guy_classic_L = "";

user string vr_fit_hand_pechenko_doomslayer_R = "";
user string vr_fit_hand_pechenko_doomslayer_L = "";


// ==== HAND-WRITTEN BELOW HERE -- genbodies.py KEEPS THIS ====
//
// Everything below this line is hand-written and genbodies.py keeps it. Anything ABOVE the
// line is deleted the next time the generator runs; it refuses rather than doing that
// silently, but the only safe place for a hand-written cvar is down here.

// The aim ray drawn while a weapon is being fitted -- the line the barrel is aligned
// against. DECLARED HERE, NOT IN THE ENGINE, and set by fit mode. ZScript cannot write an
// engine cvar outside menu code (it aborts the VM), so the engine reads this one instead;
// see the note on FitAimRayWanted in src/r_data/vr_rig.cpp. Nothing should bind this to a
// menu -- fit mode owns it.
user bool vr_fit_aimray = false;

// ------------------------------------------------------- what the body says
// The design is the owner's, out of RS_VRBody; see zscript/avatar/colour.zs.
//
//   armour_colour  the body's colour follows how much armour you HAVE:
//                  0-99 your own skins, 100-149 green, 150+ blue.
//   breathe        below breathe_below health a red tint fades in and out,
//                  slowly, faster the closer you are to dying. A sine, never
//                  a flash -- photosensitivity.
//
// Nothing ever mixes: hurt wins, so one colour only ever shows one thing.
user bool vr_avatar_armour_colour = true;
user bool vr_avatar_breathe       = true;
user int  vr_avatar_breathe_below = 33;

// ON. It was off while this used a palette translation, which draws nothing at
// all on a truecolour Source skin and hid the whole body. It now drives the
// engine's ModelTint, which the shader multiplies into the skin directly.
user bool vr_avatar_colour = true;

// ------------------------------------------------------------- the helmet
// Worn on the head and hidden from your own eyes by distance, not by a switch:
// the shader dissolves it per pixel where it is nearer than _far and it is gone
// by _near, so a mirror across the room still sees it whole. See MODELDEF.
user bool  vr_avatar_helmet = true;

// HEADLESS: the body's own head (and any helmet sculpted onto it) is removed in
// EVERY view -- mirror, spectator, co-op -- so the universal helmet above is the
// only head anyone sees (owner, 2026-10-16). Read by the engine by name
// (vr_avatar_pose.cpp AvatarHeadless). Off: the body keeps its own head for
// everyone but you, and the two bodies whose head IS a helmet wear no second one.
user bool  vr_avatar_headless = true;
user float rsa_helmet_eyefade_near = 4.0;
user float rsa_helmet_eyefade_far  = 14.0;

// --------------------------------------------------------------- the body
// THE SAME FADE, FOR THE BODY ITSELF, which never had one (owner, 2026-10-04:
// bodies "displaying their heads and helmets ... hidden from my eyes").
//
// The helmet above has faded since it was written because the helmet model
// declares a placement prefix. The bodies declared none, so the engine's test
// (models.cpp ModelEyeFadeRange) failed on its first line and every body drew
// its own head, and its own built-in helmet, straight into your view. The
// prefix is set on the avatar actor in handler.zs, one name for all of them.
//
// _far is where it STARTS to dissolve and _near is where it is gone, both in
// map units from the eye. A mirror draws from the mirror, which is far from
// the body, so it is whole there whatever these say.
//
// DEFAULT OFF (far = 0), BECAUSE A DISTANCE FADE CANNOT DO THIS JOB.
//
// Shipped at 6/18 on 2026-10-04 and the owner reported it the same week: "my
// entire body is mostly transparent. that's a new thing and i do not care for
// it." He was right and the idea was wrong, not the numbers.
//
// The measurement is distance from the EYE, and on a drawn avatar the chest is
// as close to the eye as the head is. From his own boot log: AVSCALE drew the
// body at 53.6 units with eyeHeight 71.39 and viewZ 44 -- so the head spans
// roughly 0-10 units from the eye and the chest roughly 2-14. THEY OVERLAP.
// There is no near/far pair that takes the head and leaves the torso; every
// value either keeps the jaw or eats the chest. Narrowing it is not a fix.
//
// The helmet's fade above is fine and stays: a WORN helmet is a separate model
// sitting at the head, with nothing of the body at that distance to catch.
//
// The real mechanism for the body's own head is per SURFACE, which is what
// RS_VRBody did -- skin the head surface to a transparent texture and draw the
// head as a separate actor with MASTERNOSEE so mirrors still see it. That needs
// a head surface index per body, which now exists: tools/avatar/dump_surfaces.py
// prints them in the engine loader's own order. Two bodies (doomslayer_lowpoly,
// doomslayer) are a single merged surface and cannot be done that way at all.
//
// Left as a cvar rather than deleted so the mechanism stays reachable, and so
// anyone who sets it learns why it was off.
user float rsa_body_eyefade_near = 0.0;
user float rsa_body_eyefade_far  = 0.0;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// [OWNBODY] WHAT THE WEARER SEES OF HIMSELF, once the whole body is posed.
// WholeBodyIK step 9.
//
// Until the torso was actually posed, showing it from the inside was plainly
// wrong: a rigid trunk under a head that never came down reads as standing in
// a mannequin. A posed one bends at the hips with him, so looking down he
// should see his chest, belly, hips, legs and feet, and his arms attached to
// shoulders rather than floating.
//
//   0  arms only, exactly as before
//   1  the body, but only while it is actually posed (vr_body >= 1)
//   2  always
//
// A SEPARATE CVAR FROM vr_avatar_fullbody ON PURPOSE. The owner has `false`
// archived for that one, from when a rigid torso seen from inside was wrong.
// Reusing it would mean his saved preference silently hid the new body and the
// feature would look broken for the one person testing it.
//
// The engine declares these; they are repeated here so the menu can reach them
// and so a reader of this package can see what it exposes.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// ------------------------------------------------------------- the mirror size
// IN METRES, standing on the floor in front of you (owner, 2026-10-16: "a 3 meter x 2 meter
// mirror in front of me the second I press that button"). Read by mirror.zs when the mirror
// goes up. Here and not beside vr_mirror above the mark, because that block is generated.
user float vr_mirror_width  = 3.0;     // metres across
user float vr_mirror_height = 2.0;     // metres tall, bottom edge on the floor
user bool  vr_mirror_flip   = true;    // left-right flipped like a real mirror; off = camera view

// ------------------------------------------------------ the stock player sprite
// While a body is worn, the pawn's own Doom sprite is drawn only when this is above 0. It is 0:
// the world body is what you and anyone else sees (owner, 2026-10-16). Render only -- monsters
// still see and fight the pawn. handler.zs sets the pawn's VisibleCVar to this name.
user float rsa_pawn_sprite  = 0;
